content.text:
World Builder helps you build a room where people already sit and lie when the apartment loads. It does not give the live cast a command to sit on that couch.

It is an in-game map editor. You place an AI spot, pick a workspot, and a preview body plays it while you nudge the spot until the hips land on the cushion or the mattress. A community then spawns chosen characters onto those spots when that part of the apartment streams in. Two couch spots and one bed spot is exactly the scene you described, and the preview is the fiddly lining-up pass with a picture instead of a guess.

Those people belong to the apartment, not to a place command. They show up because the world edit is loaded, on the community’s schedule, as the character records you baked in. Changing who is there for a campaign beat, a promo, or a machinima shot means editing the build again. They are not the tagged people `place` and `clear` already move. The couch and chair entries in the related interaction framework are prompts for V.

It also asks for the latest ArchiveXL, Codeware, CET, RED4ext, and redscript, plus WolvenKit to export the edit. This project is pinned to the versions already in the stack, so installing it means checking that pin before anything else.

For a shot that changes, the path is still a mark and a clip on the people we spawn. World Builder is the tool when the apartment itself should contain that scene every time you walk in.

That worry matches a fork the project already made. I’ll check the written boundary so the answer stays on the table, not the quest-mod path.

Those mods are a quest mod. The table is the other job, and the apartment question is what made them look like the same job.

Native Interactions, sit-anywhere, and World Builder teach the city to be a place. A couch gets a sit prompt, a bed gets a sleep spot, a community spawns people onto those spots when the room loads, and WolvenKit bakes it into the sector. Every new room is another set of nodes, refs, and exports. That is how you build an apartment people can live in. It is also how a year disappears into furniture.

The table treats Cyberpunk 2077 as a stage. The rules and the dice decide what happened. The game shows it. A person is a name, a mark, a facing, and a held pose. A jump cut hides the teleport, so nobody walks to the chair, opens the door, or uses the couch. A negotiation is people standing in a wedge with a talk pose. A fight is the same people in an aim or a kneel, then a cut to one of them on the ground. A promo is the same list with a camera. The apartment couch is optional set dressing: one saved mark if a shot needs it, and the shot still works if they are standing in front of it.

Chasing the interaction mods would mean maintaining Night City's furniture so the puppets have something to use. The puppets do not need the furniture. They need to appear, hold still, change pose, and disappear, on command, without taking the street with them. That is the spawn control from earlier, and it is the whole of what the stage has to do.

the problem is that chat will be driving on the fly decisions so id have to be ready for anything. i feel like that complicates things. itd be one thing taking a campaign that already played out and representing it the way you describe because we'd follow a single deterministic path. but what we're doing seems a bit more complex
</user_query>
Chat making the calls live is the actual product, so the bound on “anything” matters. I’ll read how a vote becomes a shot.

Live chat does not make the stage open-ended. Chat picks the next step on a path that was written before the stream. The pictures for those steps already exist. A replay and a live gig use the same shots. What changes is who chooses the branch, and when.

Each window offers at most four actions. They are the overlap of what that seat can do, what this spot allows, and what the rules currently permit, with one defensive option always in the list. Solo, Netrunner, Tech, and Face do not share a verb list. A balcony, a back room, and an alley do not share a tag list. Free text is sorted onto one of those four, or dropped as chatter. "Smoke the boss from the left column" can win the vote only by landing on an option that was already on screen. It does not create a fifth verb, and it does not require a new piece of the city.

The dice then pick a result class: miss, hit, crit, kill, and the few others the rules actually emit. Each class has a beat written ahead of time. A beat is a short timeline of cuts, poses, effects, and a kill. The people are already standing on marks. The cut hides the teleport. A hit is the aim pose, a muzzle flash, a cut to the target. A kill is that plus the target on the ground. A Face deal is the talk pose and a different cut. None of those shots ask the couch to be usable.

So "ready for anything" means ready for any legal option on the current node, then any result class that option can roll. Season 0 is five soundstages and reusable gig templates. Variety is who the enemy is, what the squads were told to want, and which lifepath hook is in play. It is not a new animation for each sentence in chat.

The live part is the tally and the roll, both recorded. After the stream, the event log can play the same gig back, because the votes and the dice are the path. The stage never had to discover the path while the bodies were on it. The apartment, the sit prompts, and the baked communities are a different product. They would matter if chat could invent a place and a verb. The table does not let chat do that.

Yes. The last stretch has been proving that people can stand on marks. That does not tell you whether a stranger can watch a decision and know what happened. That is the question that shelved this, and no recent mod answered it.

The roadmap already treats that as the first gate: four people, one short sequence, wide shot, a shot fired, someone down, wide again, captured so you can watch it back. A later gate is the real playtest, with chat and a private channel and most of an hour. Doing that now would bury the question under votes, dice, and plumbing. If you cannot make one exchange read with your own hands, chat will not make it read.

Bound it so it stays a test. One place you can already stand in, with almost nobody else around. The people you can already spawn, plus one opponent. Four pictures, because those are the pictures a round actually shows: a talk, a miss, a hit, a kill. Many menu options share one of those pictures. Play them in order, as cuts, with the bodies already on their marks. Record it. Show it to someone who has not been in these sessions and ask what happened. If they can say it back, the stage is real enough to keep building. If they cannot, the fallback already written is the honest result: cut away on the impact, play the sound, put a banner up, and reveal the body already down.

Original characters, the apartment couch, sit prompts, and a full gig are later costs. They do not change whether a held pose and a cut can carry a beat. The opportunity is still there. The strategic move is to spend the next block of work on that one recorded exchange and let it fail in the open if it fails.

Yes. The chat, the dice, the seats, and the consequences can all run with the game switched off. A cut-together gunfight never touches the thing you are worried about.

A shot that reads only proves the illustration. A campaign is the hour around it: four seats with different things to want, a vote that is visible while it is happening, a roll you can check, a result that changes the next choice, a death that stays dead, and a lull where the crew spends what it earned. That loop is already designed to run against a fake stage and a flat tactical picture. The bodies in Night City are a skin on top of a gig that has to be worth driving first.

The slice that matches that is one gig, played, not filmed. A briefing, one approach, one encounter with the four-option windows, an extraction, a payout, and one downtime poll. Someone dies and is replaced, so permanence is in the hour and not in a paragraph. Friends in a test channel will tell you if it is compelling. A simulated crowd will tell you if a window goes quiet, if a seat has nothing real to do, or if the gig collapses into the same choice every time. Either one is enough to fail the idea in the open. The game footage can stay a map until that hour works.

What that slice still will not prove is whether the cuts make the roll feel like it happened in the city. That question waits. It is smaller than the one in front of you, and it is the one the last two weeks were accidentally answering.

The game stays on. A loop that only runs on a map is a board game, and a board game is not this show.

A vertical slice here is one gig, watched in the city, from briefing to payout. Someone chooses among the four options, the dice settle it, and the next picture is the people already standing in that place, in the pose that result calls for. Then the next choice is different because of what just happened. Someone dies and is still dead when the payout comes. Downtime happens in the same hour, in the same world. You are looking at Night City the whole time.

That does not require the finished machine. Chat can be a few people typing, or you reading the options out loud. The cuts can be clumsy. The poses can be the few that already hold. An overlay can sit on a second screen. What cannot be faked is the handoff: a real choice, a real roll, and a picture in the game that a viewer can connect to that roll before the next choice appears. If that hour is dull, more spawn work will not save it. If that hour holds attention while the pictures are still rough, the campaign is real enough to keep building.

content.text:
No. Nothing on the market has Night City’s weight and also lets you direct the people in it.

Cyberpunk 2077 still has the world, and it still does not have a director. REDmod is the official tool, and it is a compiler: scripts, tweaks, sounds, animations, packed before launch. It does not give you a live hand on a person, a chair, or a camera. The ceiling is the same stack you already walked into. CET, the appearance menu, and World Builder. That is why it still feels like a frankenstein. The tech you were waiting on did not arrive. CDPR shipped a way to install mods faster, not a way to run the city.

The games that actually let you tell a person to use a chair ship the editor, and then the content is yours to build. Fallout 4 and Starfield have that. A chair is a marker, an NPC package can sit in it, a scene can fire when you say so. You pay for it by authoring the quest, and the picture is not Night City. The Witcher 3 has an official kit from the same company and the wrong world. GTA V is the nearest dense city, and driving its people still means a script hook and a pile of tools Rockstar does not support. Life sims and Fortnite-style editors will sit a character on furniture because you built the furniture.

What you want is three things that have never been one product. A finished city people already recognize. A live hand on whoever is standing in it. A campaign that chat can steer while that city shows the result. Every alternative keeps two and drops one. You keep the city and lose the hand. You take the hand and spend years building the city, or you accept a different city. The compromise is not a gap that a patch is about to close. It is how these games are sold.

# ADR-014 — The project is frozen

**Context.** Place and clear of one named person already work (ArcadeLink 0.1.12). The user wanted full spawn control for a campaign, a promo, and machinima, including people sitting and lying on real furniture, with chat choosing the path while the game is on. Feature-by-feature puppetry, World Builder, Native Interactions, and sit-anywhere mods were weighed against that. A recorded gunfight was rejected as too small. A board-game loop with the game off was rejected as not the show.

The same limit shelved the project once before. REDmod is still a compiler for scripts, tweaks, sounds, and animations. It is not a live hand on a person, a chair, or a camera. The working ceiling is still CET, the appearance menu, and World Builder. No other current game has Night City's weight and that hand. The ones that can seat a person ship an editor, and then the city is yours to build.

**Decision.**

- Development stops. Do not resume pose, furniture, a campaign slice, or further mod stacking unless the user reopens.
- The design already written stays written. Gates stay defined. They are not in progress.
- The last verified cast state stands. ArcadeLink 0.1.12 can place and clear one named person on an empty rank, file, or wedge mark. Tags survive a reload. V is not moved. The street is not swept. The occupied-mark slide (R-16) stays recorded and is not being fixed.
- The stack pin is unchanged (ADR-012).

**Rejected.** Treating a map-only loop as the vertical slice. Treating one action sequence as proof of a campaign. Switching games to escape the compromise.

# ADR-014 — The project is frozen

**Context.** Place and clear of one named person already work (ArcadeLink 0.1.12). The user wanted full spawn control for a campaign, a promo, and machinima, including people sitting and lying on real furniture, with chat choosing the path while the game is on. Feature-by-feature puppetry, World Builder, Native Interactions, and sit-anywhere mods were weighed against that. A recorded gunfight was rejected as too small. A board-game loop with the game off was rejected as not the show.

The same limit shelved the project once before. REDmod is still a compiler for scripts, tweaks, sounds, and animations. It is not a live hand on a person, a chair, or a camera. The working ceiling is still CET, the appearance menu, and World Builder. No other current game has Night City's weight and that hand. The ones that can seat a person ship an editor, and then the city is yours to build.

**Decision.**

- Development stops. Do not resume pose, furniture, a campaign slice, or further mod stacking unless the user reopens.
- The design already written stays written. Gates stay defined. They are not in progress.
- The last verified cast state stands. ArcadeLink 0.1.12 can place and clear one named person on an empty rank, file, or wedge mark. Tags survive a reload. V is not moved. The street is not swept. The occupied-mark slide (R-16) stays recorded and is not being fixed.
- The stack pin is unchanged (ADR-012).

**Rejected.** Treating a map-only loop as the vertical slice. Treating one action sequence as proof of a campaign. Switching games to escape the compromise.
